messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: HIGH - GPU pool r3 memory_pressure > 92% (kvcache saturation suspected). Page sent to @oncall-1 and @maya. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-memory

pagerduty: Incident created (PD-19876). Trigger: gpu_memory_pressure. Escalation path: oncall -> eng-sre -> eng-runtime.

oncall-1: acked via PD. I'm on it, pulling recent allocator logs.

maya: jumping in, tagging dennis for runtime hints. any recent deploys to r3?

dennis: there was a canary yesterday that enabled aggressive kv prefetching (v2.9.4). I rolled it to 10% but maybe a regression.

lee: noticing elevated evictions in r3 from autoscaler, plus a spike in cold-start tokenization. metric snapshot: `gpu_kvcache_evictions: 14k/min` `cuda_alloc_failures: 3/min`

maya: running remote shell on one affected node `r3-node-7`:
```
$ sudo journalctl -u redwood-runtime -n 200 | grep -i kvcache
2026-03-15T03:05:21 runtime[4578]: kv_cache: prefetch miss storm: client_id=svc-ingest
2026-03-15T03:05:22 runtime[4578]: cuda alloc failed: out of memory, tried=1, free=120MB
```

ops-bot: Suggested mitigation: scale down prefetch threads via flag `--kv-prefetch=0` on runtime, and drain heavy clients. See `ops playbook gpu-memory-pressure`.

maya: quick mitigation: patched runtime config on r3 pool to `--kv-prefetch=0` for canary nodes, restarting pods now (kubectl rollout restart).

oncall-1: restarted pod r3-runtime-7, watching metrics.

dennis: also lowering `max_prefetch_concurrency` at edge LB to 2 to slow the storm. Pushing change now.

lee: metrics showing immediate improvement on restarted node: evictions down to 600/min, free GPU up to ~28% from 6%.

pagerduty: PD update: Incident PD-19876 status: acknowledged, partial mitigation applied.

maya: coordinating customer impact check. internal dashboard shows embed-api 500s up ~3% over baseline between 03:04-03:12 UTC, latency p95 increased ~120ms. No major customer-facing outages reported by support yet.

oncall-1: notified support to watch for spikes, posted status to #customer-impact.

lee: found logs indicating a small subset of requests causing unbounded prefetch for long contexts; we should whitelist/blacklist until fix. `req_id=abcd-1234` examples attached.

dennis: creating a hotfix PR to gate prefetch on token-length heuristics and to add backpressure to kv prefetch. ETA ~20m.

ops-bot: If mitigation holds for 15m, recommend moving to 'monitoring' and perform controlled rollback of prefetch change on remaining nodes.

maya: agree. will leave canary nodes downscoped and slowly roll the change to remaining r3 nodes after PR merged.

oncall-1: handing off to night oncall (sre_tara) at 03:30 UTC. summary: PD-19876 - kvcache prefetch storm from v2.9.4 causing GPU mem pressure across r3 pool. Immediate mitigation: disabled kv-prefetch on canaries, lowered prefetch concurrency at LB, restarted affected pods. Customer impact: small spike in 500s (~3%), latency p95 +120ms. followups: merge hotfix PR, add token-length gate, add synthetic monitors for prefetch bursts.

sre_tara: acked handoff. I will monitor dashboards for next 2 hours and coordinate with dennis for hotfix rollout tomorrow morning PST. please add any more context here. :handshake:
